quotes.text: “That’s AC, the firm dog. He lives here.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “How many lawyers are in your firm?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Just two. It’s a boutique firm. I’m the junior partner. Oscar Finley’s the senior partner.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “And what kind of work would David do here?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We specialize in injury and death cases.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Like all those guys who advertise on television?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We don’t do TV,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Do you think he’ll remember any of this in the morning?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Hard to say,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look, really none of my business and all, but does he do this often? He says he wants to work here, and, well, we need to know if he might have a problem with the bottle.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “He doesn’t drink much at all. Never has. He might occasionally at a party, but he works too hard to drink much. And since I rarely touch the stuff, we don’t keep it around the house.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Just curious. I’ve had my problems.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m sorry.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, it’s okay. I’ve been sober for sixty days now.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I suppose I should take him home.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, I suppose. Or he could stay here with the dog.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s what he deserves, you know? He should wake up in the morning here on the sofa, still dressed, a splitting headache, upset stomach, parched tongue, and have no idea where he is. That would serve him right, don’t you think?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It would, but I’d rather not clean up after him again.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “He’s already—”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Twice. Once on the porch, once in the restroom.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m so sorry.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It’s okay. But he needs to go home.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I know. Let’s get him up.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look, I think I have most of the major plot points, but just a few details might help. Where was the bar?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Abner’s. A few blocks from the office.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Been there before?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, great place, though. I’ll take you there sometime.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sure. Why not tomorrow? And you walked into Abner’s at what time this morning?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Between 7:30 and 8:00. I fled the office, ran a few blocks, found Abner’s.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “And started drinking?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh yes.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Recall what you consumed?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, let’s see.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “For breakfast, I had four of Abner’s special Bloody Marys. They’re really good. Then I had a plate of onion rings and several pints of beer. Miss Spence showed up, and I had two of her Pearl Harbors, wouldn’t want to do that again.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Miss Spence?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yep. She shows up every day, same stool, same drink, same everything.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “And you liked her?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I adored her. Very cute, hot.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I see. She married?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, a widow. She’s ninety-four and worth a few billion.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Any other women?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh no, just Miss Spence. She left sometime around noon, and, uh, let’s see. I had a burger and fries for lunch, then back to the beer, and then at some point I took a nap.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You blacked out?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Whatever.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “So how did you get from the bar to that law office back there?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A cab. Paid the guy forty bucks.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Where did you get into the cab?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Don’t remember that.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Now we’re making progress. And the big question: How did you find Finley &amp; Figg?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I have no idea.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I have a question,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I have lots of questions,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m sure you do, but I don’t want to talk now. Save it for tomorrow when I’m sober, okay? It’s not fair to hammer me now when I’m drunk.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Fair enough. What’s your question?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Are your parents, by chance, in our home at this moment?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes. They’ve been there for some time. They’re very concerned.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “How nice. Look, I’m not walking into our home if your parents are there, got that? I don’t want them to see me like this. Understand?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “They love you, David. You scared all of us.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Why is everyone so scared? I texted you twice and said I was okay. You knew I was alive. What’s all the panic about?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Don’t get me started.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “So I had a bad day, what’s the big deal?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A bad day?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Actually, it was a pretty good day, come to think of it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Why don’t we argue tomorrow, David? Isn’t that what you asked?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, but I’m not getting out of the car until they leave. Please.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, good morning, Ms. Gibson,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Good morning, Mr. Figg,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “And what brings you here so early?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I met David’s wife last night,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Very cute and nice. Said he doesn’t drink much, maybe blows it out from time to time. I think the pressure gets to him occasionally. I know that’s my story. Always the pressure.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What time did she get him?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “After eight. He walked out of here, even asked if he could drive. She said no.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Was she upset?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “She was pretty cool. Relieved more than anything else. The big question is whether he’ll remember anything. And if he does, then the question is whether he’ll find us again. Will he really walk away from the big firm and the big bucks? I got my doubts.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I could use him, though,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You ever hear of a cholesterol drug called Krayoxx?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’ve already asked me this.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It causes heart attacks and strokes, and the truth is just now coming out. The first wave of litigation is unfolding, could be tens of thousands of cases before it’s over. The mass tort lawyers are all over it. I talked to a big firm in Fort Lauderdale yesterday. They’ve already filed a class action and are looking for more cases.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Anyway, I’m spending the next few days looking for Krayoxx cases, and I could sure use some help. Are you listening, Ms. Gibson?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sure.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “How many names are in our client database, both active and retired?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We have about two hundred active files,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “And retired?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Last time I checked, the computer showed three thousand files retired since 1991. I don’t know what’s upstairs.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Three thousand,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Here’s the plan, Ms. Gibson. I have drafted a letter that I want you to print on our stationery. It goes to every client, current and past, active and retired. Every name in our client database.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Threats.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Has Oscar seen this?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Not yet. Pretty good, huh?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This for real?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh, it’s so real, Ms. Gibson. This is our biggest moment.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Another gold mine?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Bigger than a gold mine.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “And you want to send three thousand letters?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yep, you print ’em, I’ll sign ’em, we’ll stuff ’em, and they go out in today’s mail.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s over a thousand bucks in postage.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Ms. Gibson, the average Krayoxx case will generate something like $200,000 in attorneys’ fees, and that’s on the low side. Could be as high as $400,000 per case. If we can find ten cases, the math gets real easy.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “All right,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s all this?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “The sounds of capitalism at work,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What the hell does that mean?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Protecting the rights of the injured. Serving our clients. Purging the market of dangerous products. Bringing corporate wrongdoers to justice.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Chasing ambulances,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You gotta read this, Oscar,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is brilliant.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Come on, Wally, not again. How many of these are you sending out?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Three thousand. Our entire client list.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What? Think of the postage. Think of the wasted time. Here we go again. You’ll spend the next month running around chirping about Krayoxx this and Krayoxx that, and you’ll waste a hundred hours looking for worthless cases, and on and on. We’ve been here before, Wally, come on. Do something productive.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Like what?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Like go hang out in an emergency room somewhere, wait for a real case to come in. I don’t have to tell you how to find good cases.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m tired of that crap, Oscar. I wanna make some money. Let’s hit it big for a change.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “My wife’s been taking the drug for two years. Loves it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Did you tell her to stop, that it’s killing people?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Of course not.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, well, if it ain’t Mr. Harvard,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m back.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m surprised you could find us.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It wasn’t easy. Where’s my office?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, uh, let’s see. I’m not sure we have one. Perhaps we should ask the two bosses about this.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “So they’re here?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, they usually start the day with a round of bickering.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I see.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look, Harvard, are you sure you know what you’re doing? This is another world. You’re taking a plunge here, leaving the fancy life of corporate law for the bush leagues. You might get hurt out here, and you sure won’t make any money.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ve done the big-firm thing, Ms. Gibson, and I’ll jump off a bridge before I go back. Just give me a little room somewhere to park myself, and I’ll figure it out.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, good morning, David. You look surprisingly healthy.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Thank you, and I’d like to apologize for my appearance yesterday.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You caught me at the tail end of a rather unusual episode, but it was nonetheless a very important day in my life. I quit the big firm, and here I am, ready to go to work.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What type of work do you have in mind?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “For the past five years, I’ve labored in the dungeon of bond underwriting, with emphasis on second- and third-tier aftermarket spreads, primarily for foreign multinational corporations that prefer to avoid paying taxes anywhere in the world. If you have no idea what that is, then don’t worry. No one else does either. What it means is that a small team of us idiots labored fifteen hours a day in a room with no windows creating paperwork, and more paperwork. I’ve never seen the inside of a courtroom, or a courthouse for that matter, never met a judge when he was wearing a robe, never offered a hand to help a person who needed a real lawyer. To answer your question, Mr. Finley, I’m here to do anything. Think of me as a rookie fresh out of law school who doesn’t know his ass from a hole in the ground. But I’m a quick study.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “There is some space upstairs,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ll take it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It’s a junk room,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ll take it,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I haven’t been up there in years,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I like it,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look, David, we can offer a small salary, but you’re gonna have to generate your own fees. And this won’t be easy, at least initially.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s the deal?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We can pay a thousand bucks a month, and you keep half of what you bring in. After six months, we’ll reevaluate.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It will be rough at first, lots of competition out there on the streets.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We can toss some files your way,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We’ll give you a piece of the Krayoxx litigation,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “The what?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Never mind,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look, guys,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ve made a very nice salary for the past five years. I’ve spent a lot, but there’s a chunk in the bank. Don’t worry about me. I’ll take the deal.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Say, David, I’m due in court at eleven. Divorce court. I doubt you’ve ever been there, so I was thinking you could tag along and I’ll introduce you to the judge.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Let’s go.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Is that your Audi SUV?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It is.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Do you mind driving? I’ll do the talking.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sure.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look, David, the truth is that I got a DUI a year ago and my license is suspended. There, I said it. I believe in being honest.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Okay. You’ve certainly seen me drunk enough.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I have indeed. But your cute wife told me you’re not much of a drinker. I, on the other hand, have quite a history. I’m sober for sixty-one days now. Every day is a challenge. I go to AA, and I’ve rehabbed several times. What else do you want to know?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I didn’t bring this up.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oscar, he has a few strong ones every night. Believe me, with his wife, he needs them, but he keeps it under control. Some people are like that, you know. They can stop with two or three. They can skip a few days, even weeks, no problem. Others can’t stop until they black out, kinda like you yesterday.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Thanks, Wally. Where are we headed, by the way?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “The Daley Center downtown, 50 West Washington. Me, I do fine for a while. I’ve quit four or five times, you know?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “How would I know that?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Anyway, enough of the booze.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s wrong with Oscar’s wife?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Tough woman, man. One of these people who grew up in a nicer part of town, father wore a suit and tie to work, as opposed to a uniform, so she was raised to believe she’s better than most. A real snot. She made a major mistake when she married Oscar because she figured he was a lawyer, right? Lawyers make lots of money, right? Not exactly. Oscar has never made enough to satisfy her, and she hammers him relentlessly because she wants more money. I loathe the woman. You won’t meet her, because she refuses to set foot in the office, which suits me just fine.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Why not get a divorce?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s what I’ve been saying for years. Me, I got no problem with divorce. Been down that road four times.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Four times?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yep, and every trip was worth the hassle. You know what they say—the reason divorce is so expensive is because it’s worth it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Are you married now?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Nope, back on the prowl,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “blatant solicitation”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I would be there right now,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Which one?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “The Trust Tower.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I was in the Sears Tower one summer, a clerk, after my second year of law school. Martin &amp; Wheeler. And I thought that’s what I wanted.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What happened?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Couldn’t pass the bar exam.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’re not going to miss it, are you?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, I’m breaking into a sweat right now, just looking at the building. I don’t want to get any closer.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Take a left on Washington. We’re almost there.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Have you really never seen the inside of a courtroom?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Not since law school.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Unbelievable. What have you been doing for the past five years?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You don’t want to know.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m sure you’re right about that. This is us,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Circuit Court of Cook County—Divorce Division, Hon. Charles Bradbury.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Who’s Bradbury?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’re about to meet him.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is known as an open day, as opposed to a trial day. Generally speaking, you can get motions granted, routine matters approved, crap like that. That lady over there in the short yellow dress is our beloved client DeeAnna Nuxhall, and she thinks she’s about to get another divorce.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Another?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ve done one already. This would be my second. I think she has a prior.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Looks like a stripper.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Nothing would surprise me.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Mr. Figg,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s up?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We have a new associate, Your Honor,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Meet David Zinc.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Welcome to my courtroom,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “David’s been with a big firm downtown. Now he wants to see the real side of justice,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You won’t learn much from Figg,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “He went to Harvard Law School,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Then what are you doing here?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Got sick of the big firm,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We have a slight problem here, Judge. My client is the lovely DeeAnna Nuxhall, fourth row left, in the yellow dress.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “She looks familiar.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yep, she was here about a year ago, second or third divorce.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Same dress, I think.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, I think so too. Same dress, but the boobs are new.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You getting any?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Not yet.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s the problem?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I haven’t been paid. She owes three hundred bucks, and I can’t seem to squeeze it out of her.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What parts have you squeezed?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Ha-ha. She refuses to pay, Judge.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I need a closer look.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Basic no-fault divorce, right, Mr. Figg?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s correct, Your Honor,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Is everything in order?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, except for the small matter of my fee.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I just noticed that,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It looks as though there is a balance of $300, right?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s correct, Your Honor.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Are you prepared to take care of the fee, Ms. Nuxhall?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, Your Honor,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “But I’ll have to wait until next week. You see, I’m getting married this Saturday, and, well, I just can’t swing it right now.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It’s my experience, Ms. Nuxhall, in divorce cases the fees are never paid after the fact. I expect my lawyers to be taken care of, to be paid, before I sign the final orders. What is the total fee, Mr. Figg?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Six hundred. She paid half up front.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Six hundred?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s a very reasonable fee, Ms. Nuxhall. Why haven’t you paid your lawyer?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m not granting this divorce today, Ms. Nuxhall. You get your lawyer paid, then I’ll sign the papers. You understand this?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Please.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m sorry, but I run a tight ship. I insist that all obligations be met—alimony, child support, legal fees. It’s just $300. Go borrow it from a friend.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ve tried, Your Honor, but—”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Please. I hear this all the time. You’re excused.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Anything else?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “One more, Judge. Joannie Brenner. No-fault, complete property settlement, no children, and, most important, my fee has been paid in full.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Get her up here.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m not sure I’m cut out for divorce law,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Great, you’ve been to court one time now, for less than an hour, and you’re already streamlining your practice,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Do most judges do what Bradbury just did?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What? You mean protect his lawyers? No, most judges have forgotten what it’s like to be in the trenches. As soon as they put on the black robe, they forget. Bradbury, he’s different. He remembers what a bunch of creeps we represent.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “So what happens now? Will DeeAnna get her divorce?”

quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You can’t work for these people, David. Come on. Quit Rogan if you want, but let’s find a different firm somewhere. These two clowns are a couple of crooks. What about ethics?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I doubt if they spend much time discussing ethics.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Why not look for a nice midsized firm somewhere, with nice people who don’t carry guns and chase ambulances and swap labor for sex?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s my specialty, Helen?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Something to do with bonds.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Right. I know a lot about high-yield, long-term bonds issued by foreign governments and corporations. That’s all I know about the law because that’s all I’ve done for the past five years. Put that on a résumé, and the only people who might call are a handful of eggheads at other large firms, just like Rogan, who might be in need of someone like me.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “But you can learn.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Of course I can, but no one will hire a five-year lawyer at a nice salary and put him in kindergarten. They demand experience, and I don’t have it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “So Finley & Figg is the only place you can work?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Or someplace like it. I’ll treat it like a seminar for a year or two, then maybe open my own shop.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Great. One day on the job and you’re already thinking about leaving.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Not really. I love the place.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’ve lost your mind.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, and it’s so liberating.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “others to be named later,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Chicago Attorney Attacks Varrick Labs over Krayoxx.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “self-described mass tort specialist.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “boutique firm”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “looking forward to a fair trial before an impartial jury to clear our good name.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “non-death”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We got four death cases here, brand-new ones, and we gotta sign ’em up right now. Are you in, Oscar?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sure, I’ll take one,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Thank you. Now, Ms. Gibson, there’s a black lady who lives on Nineteenth, not far from you, Bassitt Towers, number three. She says it’s safe.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I will not go to Bassitt Towers,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I can practically hear the gunfire from my apartment.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s my point. It’s right down the street from you. You could stop by on the way home.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I will not.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Can’t you see what’s happening here, damn it? These people are begging us to take their cases, cases that are worth millions of bucks. There could be a huge settlement within a year. We’re on the verge of something big here, and you, as always, couldn’t care less.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I will not risk my neck for this law firm.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Great. So when Varrick settles and the cash pours in, you will forgo your share of the bonus. That’s what you’re telling us?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What bonus?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, well, how quickly we forget. Remember the Sherman case last year, Ms. Gibson? Nice little car wreck, a rear-ender. State Farm paid sixty grand. We took a third, a nice fee of twenty thousand for good ol’ Finley & Figg. We paid some bills. I took seven grand, Oscar took seven, and we gave you a thousand bucks cash under the table. Didn’t we, Oscar?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, and we’ve done it before,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “How much of a bonus?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Come on, Ms. Gibson,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I have no idea.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What do I tell this poor woman?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I talked to her an hour ago, name’s Pauline Sutton, age sixty-two. Her forty-year-old son, Jermaine, died of a heart attack seven months ago, said he was a bit on the heavy side, took Krayoxx for four years to lower his cholesterol. A charming lady but also a grieving mother. Take one of our brand-new Krayoxx contracts for legal services, explain it to her, sign her up. Piece of cake.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What if she has questions about the lawsuit and settlement?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Make an appointment and get her in here. I’ll answer her questions. What’s important is getting her signed up. We’ve created a hornet’s nest here in Chicago. Every half-assed ambulance chaser in the business is now loose on the streets looking for Krayoxx victims. Time is of the essence. Can you do it, Ms. Gibson?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I suppose.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Thank you so much. Now, I suggest we all hit the streets.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You got five minutes. My boss is yelling back there.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You told me on the phone that your mother died six months ago, heart attack. She was sixty-six and took Krayoxx for a couple of years. How about your father?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Died three years ago.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sorry. Krayoxx, perhaps?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, colon cancer.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Brothers, sisters?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “One brother who lives in Peru. He will not be involved in any of this.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Say, I just talked to another lawyer.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh, really. What’s his name?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “He said he was a Krayoxx expert, and he could get us a million bucks, no sweat. Is that true?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “He’s lying. If he promised you a million bucks, then he’s an idiot. We can’t promise anything in the way of money. What we can promise is that we’ll provide the best legal representation you can find.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sure, sure, but I like the idea of a lawyer telling me how much I might get, know what I mean?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We can get you a lot more than a million bucks,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Now we’re talking. How long will this take?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A year, maybe two,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look this over. It’s a contract between our firm and you as the legal representative of your mother’s estate.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Nothing up front, right?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh no, we front the litigation expenses.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Forty percent for you guys is pretty steep.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s the industry average. All standard. Any lawyer doing mass torts who’s worth his salt is getting 40 percent. Some want 50, but not us. I think 50’s unethical.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I guess so,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Great, Adam, good move and welcome aboard. We’ll add this case to our lawsuit and kick things into high gear. Any questions?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yeah, what should I tell this other lawyer?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Tell him you went with the best, Finley & Figg.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’re in good hands, Adam,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Seriously?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I guess that remains to be seen, doesn’t it?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We’ll know when the big check gets here. You promised more than a million, Mr. Figg, and I take you at your word.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You won’t be sorry.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “See you,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That was easy.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You just guaranteed the guy something over a million. Is that wise?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No. But if that’s what it takes, then that’s what it takes. Here’s how it works, young David. You sign ’em up, get ’em on board, keep ’em happy, and when there’s money on the table, they’ll forget about what you said up front. Say, for example, a year from now Varrick gets sick of its Krayoxx mess and throws in the towel. Let’s say our new pal Adam here is due less than a million, pick a number—$750,000. Now, do you really believe that loser will walk away from that much money?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Probably not.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Exactly. He’ll be one happy boy, and he’ll forget about anything we said today. That’s how it works.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Say, you got plans for dinner? I’m starving.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yeah, my wife’s waiting for a late snack.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What a great idea,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m sorry.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look at those people. What’s the average weight?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I have no idea.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Neither do I, but if I’m a bit pudgy at 240, those folks are well over 400 pounds.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’re losing me, Wally.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look at the obvious, David. This place is packed with grossly overweight people, half of whom are probably on Krayoxx. I’ll bet if I yelled out right now, ‘Who’s on Krayoxx?’ half of these poor bastards would raise their hands.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: ‘Who’s on Krayoxx?’
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Don’t do that.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m not, but don’t you see my point?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You want to start handing out cards?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, smart-ass, but there must be a way to screen these people for Krayoxx users.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “But they’re not dead yet.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It won’t be long. Look, we can add them to our second lawsuit of non-death cases.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m missing something here, Wally. Help me. Aren’t we required to prove, at some point, that the drug actually causes some type of damage?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sure, and we’ll prove it later when we hire our experts. Right now, the important thing is to get everybody signed up. It’s a horse race out here, David. We gotta figure out a way to screen these folks and sign them up.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Frank Schmidt, age fifty-two when he succumbed last year to a massive stroke. I spoke with his widow, Agnes.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Look, Wally, I really would like to get home and see my wife. I haven’t seen her much in the past five years. Time to catch up.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “She’s very cute. I don’t blame you.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Frankly,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “between the two of us, I would have handled it differently, but Mr. Finley comes from the old school.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Meaning what?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “He’s pretty chauvinistic. The husband is the head of the house, keeper of all assets, the only decision maker, you know the type. If the man wants to hide things from his wife, nothing wrong with that. Me, I’m much more liberated.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “But it’s too late,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “The will has been written. Now it’s going to probate.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “True, Millie, but things will work out. Your husband left his baseball cards to his son, but he left you with a beautiful lawsuit.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A beautiful what?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You know, the Krayoxx thing.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh, that. Yes, I’m not too happy with that either. I’ve talked to another lawyer, and he says you’re in over your head, says you’ve never handled a case like this.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Why are you talking to other lawyers?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Because he called me the other night. I checked him out online. He’s in a big firm with offices all over the country, and all they do is sue drug companies. I’m thinking about hiring him.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Don’t do that, Millie. These guys are famous for signing up a thousand cases, then screwing their clients. You’ll never talk to him again, just some young paralegal in the back room. It’s a scam, I swear it is. You can always get me on the phone.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I don’t want to talk to you on the phone, or in person either.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Please, Millie.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ll think about it, Figg, but I’m not happy.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A 2 man ham and egg operation on Preston, Southwest Side; advertises for quickie divorces, DUIs, the usual criminal, domestic, injury practice; no record of any filings in federal court in the past 10 years; no record of jury trials in state court in past 10 years, no bar association activity; they do occasionally go to court—Figg has either 2 or 3 DUIs in past 12 years; firm was once sued for sexual harassment, settled.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “These guys have no trial experience, yet they filed a $100 million lawsuit against the third-largest pharmaceutical company in the world?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Correct.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Insane! What’s behind this?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Krayoxx stampede. It’s the latest and hottest bad drug in the country; mass tort bar is in frenzy. Finley & Figg probably hopes to ride coattails all the way to a settlement.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Keep digging.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “The lawsuit is signed by Finley & Figg, but also a third lawyer—David E. Zinc, former associate at Rogan Rothberg; I called a friend there—said Zinc cracked up, bolted ten days ago, somehow landed out there at FF; no litigation experience; guess he found the right place.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Let’s watch this case closely.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “As always.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s the latest?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Krayoxx or Faladin?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Gee, I almost forgot about Faladin. Let’s stick to Krayoxx for the moment.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, the gates are open. Snowball’s rolling down the mountain. Pick your metaphor. All hell’s breaking loose. I chatted with Alisandros at Zell & Potter yesterday, and they’re getting flooded with new cases. He plans to push hard to establish multi-district in Florida and keep his finger on things.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Alisandros. Why do the same thieves show up at every heist?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Haven’t we paid them enough over the past twenty years?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Evidently not. He’s built his own golf course, for Zell & Potter lawyers only and a few lucky friends, and he invited me to come down and play. Eighteen holes.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Please go, Nick. We need to see how wisely our money is being invested by these thugs.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Will do. I got a phone call late yesterday afternoon from Amanda Petrocelli in Reno, says she’s hooked her a few death clients, putting together a class, and will file suit either today or tomorrow. I told her it really didn’t matter to us when she filed suit. We can expect more filings this week and next.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Krayoxx is not causing strokes and heart attacks,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I believe in this drug.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “All of us feel the same, Reuben. Our research is better than theirs, if they actually have any. Our experts are better. Our proof is better. Our lawyers will be better. Perhaps it’s time we counterattack and throw everything we have at the enemy.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “My thoughts exactly, Judy,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You guys have a strategy?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It’s evolving, but for now we go through the same motions, make the same public comments, watch and wait and see who files what and where. We look at the lawsuits, study the judges and the jurisdictions, and we pick our spot. When the stars are all aligned—the right plaintiff, the right city, the right judge—then we hire the hottest gunslinger in town and push hard for a trial.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This has backfired, you know,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Don’t forget Klervex. That cost us two billion.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is not Klervex,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Krayoxx is a much better drug, and the lawsuits are much weaker.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I agree,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I like your plan.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You look great, Mom,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Put me down,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We have some big news.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m pregnant!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You two geezers are about to be grandparents,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Tell me about your new firm, David,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh, Andy, don’t start that,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “that”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I told you on the phone,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It’s a small two-man firm with a general practice. Fifty hours a week, which gives me time to fool around with my wife and keep the family name going. You should be proud.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m delighted Helen is expecting, but I’m not sure I understand your decision. Rogan Rothberg is one of the most prestigious law firms in the world. They’ve trained judges, legal scholars, diplomats, and leaders of business and government. How can you just walk away from that?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I didn’t walk away, Dad, I ran. And I’m not going back. I hate the memories of Rogan Rothberg, and I think even less of the people.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “So, this new firm has two partners?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Two partners and now three lawyers. Plus Rochelle, the secretary, receptionist, office manager, and a lot of other things.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Support staff? Clerks, paralegals, interns?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Rochelle handles all that. It’s a small firm where we do most of our own typing and research.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “He’s actually home for dinner,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ve never seen him so happy.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You look great,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Both of you.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “These two partners, are they trial lawyers?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “They claim to be, but I have my doubts. They’re basically a couple of ambulance chasers who advertise a lot and survive on car wrecks.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What made you choose them?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That, Dad, is a long story that I will not bore you with.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh, it’s not boring,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What kind of money do they make?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ve been there three weeks. They have not shown me the books, but they’re not getting rich. And I’m sure you wanna know how much I’m making. Same answer. I don’t know. I get a piece of what I bring in the door, and I have no idea what might walk in tomorrow.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “And you’re starting a family?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, and I’ll be home for dinner with my family, and T-ball, and Cub Scouts and school plays and all the other wonderful stuff parents are supposed to do with their kids.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I was there, David, I missed very little.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, you were, but you never worked for a sweatshop like Rogan Rothberg.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We saved a lot. We’ll survive nicely, just wait and see.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m sure you will,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I haven’t started the nursery yet,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “If you’d like, we can go to a great shop around the corner and look at wallpaper.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Perfect.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Associate boot camp is just part of the routine these days, David. You survive that, make partner, and life is good.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I didn’t sign up for the Marines, Dad, and life is never good at a huge law firm like Rogan because the partners never make enough money. I know these partners. I’ve seen them. For the most part, they’re great lawyers and miserable people. I’ve quit. I’m not going back. Drop it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What type of work are you doing?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Lots of good stuff. This week I prepared a will for a lady who’s hiding her assets from her children. They suspect she inherited some money from her third husband, which she did, but they can’t seem to find it. She wants to leave everything to her FedEx deliveryman. I represent a gay couple who are trying to adopt a child in Korea. I have two deportation cases involving illegal Mexicans who were caught in a drug ring. I represent the family of a fourteen-year-old girl who’s been hooked on crack for two years and there’s no place to lock her up for rehab. A couple of drunk-driving clients.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sounds like a bunch of riffraff,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, actually, they’re real people with real problems who need help. That’s the beauty of street law—you meet the clients face-to-face, you get to know them, and, if things work out, you get to help them.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “If you don’t starve.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m not going to starve, Dad, I promise. Besides, these guys do hit the jackpot every now and then.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I know, I know. I saw them when I was practicing, and I see their cases now on appeal. Last week, we affirmed a $9 million jury verdict, a terrible case involving a brain-damaged kid who got lead poisoning from some toys. His lawyer was a sole practitioner who did a DUI for the mother. He got the case, called in a gunslinger to try it, now they’re splitting 40 percent of $9 million.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Coffee, anyone?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “One of my law clerks came across a story about the Krayoxx litigation. Saw your picture online, the one from the Tribune, with Mr. Figg. Is he a straight-up guy?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Not really,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Doesn’t look like.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Let’s just say that Wally’s complicated.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m not sure your career will be advanced if you hang around with these guys.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You could be right, Dad, but for now I’m having fun. I look forward to getting to the office. I enjoy my clients, the few that I have, and I am enormously relieved to be out of the sweatshop. Just relax a bit, okay? If this doesn’t work out, I’ll try something else.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “How did you get involved in this Krayoxx litigation?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We found some cases.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Have you researched Krayoxx?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m in the process. Have you?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, as a matter of fact. The TV ads are running in Minnesota. The drug is getting a lot of attention. Looks like another mass tort scam to me. Pile on the lawsuits until the drugmaker is facing bankruptcy, then broker a huge settlement that makes the lawyers richer and allows the manufacturer to stay in business. Lost in the shuffle is the issue of liability, not to mention what’s best for the clients.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s a pretty fair summary,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “So you’re not sold on the case?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Not yet. I’ve plowed through a thousand pages, and I’m still looking for the smoking gun, the research to prove that the drug hurts people. I’m not sure it does.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Then why did you put your name on the lawsuit?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Wally asked me, and since I’m new at the firm, I felt an obligation to join the fun. Look, Dad, there are some very powerful lawyers around the country who have filed this same lawsuit and who believe this is a bad drug. quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes, but only if you’re serious about a settlement. If you plan to walk in with some lowball scheme, then forget it. I’ll take my chances with a jury.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Please, Mr. Zinc, it’s too early to start with the threats. I assure you we recognize the gravity of this situation. Sadly, we’ve been here before. I can explain it all on Monday.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Fair enough.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Has a legal representative been appointed by the court for this child?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes. His father.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Would it be possible to have both parents on hand Monday morning?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m sure they can be there. Why?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Carl LaPorte, our CEO, would like to meet them and, on behalf of our company, offer an apology.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, first things first. I know you have a very sick boy and he is not likely to improve much. I have a four-year-old grandson, my only grandchild, and I cannot imagine what you are going through. On behalf of my company, Sonesta Games, I take full responsibility for what has happened to your son. We did not make the product, this Nasty Teeth toy, but we own the smaller company that did import it from China. Since it’s our company, it is our responsibility. Any questions?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Nothing I can say will bring back your little boy. All I can do is say I’m sorry and promise you that our company will do all that we can to help you.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Thank you,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Mr. Zinc, I suggest the parents wait in another room down the hall while we discuss matters.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Agreed,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A couple of suggestions. Let’s take off our coats and try to relax. We could be here for some time. Any objection to using first names, Mr. Zinc?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Not at all.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Good. We’re a California company, and our culture leans to the informal.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “How would you like to proceed, David?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You called the meeting.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Right, so a little background might be helpful. First, as I’m sure you know, we’re the third-largest toy company in America, sales last year of just over $3 billion.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Behind Mattel and Hasbro,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ve read all your annual reports and a ton of other stuff. I know your products, history, financials, key personnel, divisions, and long-term corporate strategy. I know who insures your company, but of course the limits of liability are not disclosed. I’m happy to sit here and chat as long as you guys would like to. I have nothing else planned for the day, and my clients have taken off from work. But to move things along, I suggest we get down to business.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sure, we’re all busy,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’ve done your homework, David, so tell us what you have in mind.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is a summary of brain damage verdicts over the past ten years, kids only. Number 1 is a $12 million verdict in New Jersey last year for a six-year-old who ingested lead by chewing on a plastic action figure. The case is on appeal. Look at Number 4—a $9 million verdict in Minnesota that was upheld on appeal last year. My father sits on the Minnesota Supreme Court and is fairly conservative when it comes to upholding large verdicts. He voted to affirm that one, as did the rest of the court. Unanimous. It was another lead-poisoning case—a kid and his toy. Number 7 involves a nine-year-old girl who nearly drowned when her foot got caught in the drain of a brand-new swimming pool at a country club in Springfield, Illinois. Jury deliberated less than an hour and awarded the family $9 million. On page 2, look at Number 13. A ten-year-old boy was hit with a piece of metal flung from a commercial Bush Hog with no chain guards. Severe brain damage. The case was tried in federal court in Chicago, and the jury awarded $5 million in actual damages and $20 million in punitive damages. The punitive award was cut to $5 million on appeal. I don’t need to go through every case, and I’m sure you guys are familiar with this territory.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It should be obvious, David, that we would like to avoid a trial and jury.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I understand, but my point is that this case has tremendous jury appeal. After the jurors spend three days looking at Thuya Khaing strapped into his high chair, they might bring back a verdict larger than any of these. That potential should be factored into our negotiations.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Got it. What is your demand?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well, a settlement should include several areas of compensation, some relatively easy to tally, others not so easy. Let’s start with the financial burden on the family to care for the child. As of now, they’re spending about $600 a month on food, medications, and diapers. Not much money, but a lot more than the family can afford. The boy needs a part-time nurse and a full-time rehab specialist to at least attempt to retrain muscles and reprogram the brain.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s his life expectancy?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No one knows. It’s a moving target. I didn’t put it in my report, because one doctor says a year or two, off the record, and another one says he could live to be an adult. I’ve talked to all the doctors, and no one thinks it’s smart to predict how long he might live. I’ve spent some time with him during the past six months, and I’ve noticed a slight improvement in some functions, very slight. I think we should negotiate as if he has twenty years left.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It’s obvious that his parents do not earn a lot of money. They live in a small, cheap apartment with two older daughters. The family needs a home, with plenty of space and a bedroom outfitted for Thuya’s special needs. Nothing elaborate—these are simple people, but they have dreams.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is our settlement proposal. First, you see the specific damages. Number 1 covers the expenses I mentioned, plus a part-time nurse at $30,000 a year, plus the mother’s lost salary of $25,000 a year because she would like to quit work and stay home with the boy. I’ve also added the cost of a new car so they can take him to and from rehab on a daily basis. I’ve rounded it off to $100,000 a year, for twenty years, for a total of $2 million. You can buy an annuity at today’s rates for $1.4 million. Rehab is a gray area because I’m not sure how long it would continue. As of today, it runs about $50,000 a year. Assuming twenty years, the annuity will cost you $700,000. Next is the issue of a new home, in a nice neighborhood, with good schools—$500,000. The next item deals with the Lakeshore Children’s Hospital. Their care saved his life and was free, at least to the family, but I think the expenses should be paid back. The hospital was reluctant to give me an estimate, but there it is—$600,000.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Moving on to the nonspecifics, I’ve listed the kid’s loss of enjoyment of life and the emotional distress of the family. I know these are vague areas, but they are compensable damages under Illinois law. I suggest the sum of $1.8 million.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A tidy sum of $5 million,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What about attorneys’ fees?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Gee, almost forgot about those,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “My fee is not taken from what the family gets. It’s extra. Thirty percent on top of what you’re looking at there, or $1.5 million.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s a nice payday,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I would like to think I could keep it all, but that will not be the case.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Six and a half million dollars,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You guys seem intent on doing what’s right,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Plus, you don’t want bad publicity, just like you don’t want to roll the dice with an unsympathetic jury.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Our image is very important,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We don’t pollute rivers or make cheap handguns or deny insurance claims or bilk the government on bad contracts. We make toys for kids. It’s just that simple. If we get the reputation for harming children, we’re dead.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Can I ask where you found these products?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We were prepared to write a check for $5 million and put this matter to rest, David, but you’re asking for a lot more than that.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We will not accept $5 million, because the case is worth twice that much. Our number is $6.5 million, take it or leave it. I’ll file the lawsuit tomorrow.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A lawsuit will take years. Can your clients afford to wait?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Some of our federal judges use this Local Rule 83:19, nicknamed the Rocket Docket, and believe me, it works. I can have this case before a jury in a year. The last case was far more complicated, and it went to trial ten months after it was filed. Yes, my clients can survive until the jury brings back the verdict.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You didn’t win that case, did you?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, I did not, but I learned a lot. I had a lousy set of facts. This time, I own the facts. By the time the jury hears everything, $6.5 million will seem like a bargain.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “We’ll offer $5 million.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’re not hearing me, Carl. It’s $6.5 million now, or a lot more a year from now.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You’re turning down $5 million for these poor Burmese immigrants?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I just turned it down, and I’m not negotiating. Your company is well insured. The $6.5 million is not coming off your bottom line.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Maybe, but the insurance premiums are not cheap.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m not haggling, Carl. Deal or no deal?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A deal.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “On the condition that this is extremely confidential,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Of course.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ll get our guys in Legal to prepare an agreement.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Not necessary,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is a settlement agreement that covers everything. It’s pretty straightforward and includes all manner of language about confidentiality. I work for a tiny law firm, but it has some complicated problems. It’s in my best interests to keep this quiet.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You had a settlement agreement prepared at $6.5 million?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You got it. Not a penny less. That’s what this case is worth.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This settlement has to be approved by the court, right?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Yes. I’ve already established a guardianship for the kid; his father is his legal representative. The court must approve the settlement, and over the years it will supervise the money. I’m required to prepare an annual accounting and meet with the judge once a year, but the file can be sealed to ensure secrecy.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You didn’t get this from me, okay?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What is it?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A list of other products, mainly toys, with histories of lead poisoning. Most were made in China, but there are some from Mexico, Vietnam, and Pakistan. Made somewhere else, but imported here by U.S. companies.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I see. And might these companies be your competitors?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You got it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Thanks.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Good luck.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This must be important,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Indeed it is,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You guys remember that lead-poisoning case I mentioned back a few months ago?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Well,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “there has been an interesting development.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Do tell,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This morning, I met with the CEO and other top executives from the company, and we reached a settlement.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “The attorneys’ fees are $1.5 million,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is a proposed partnership agreement for the new law firm of Finley, Figg & Zinc.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “An equal partnership, a three-way split of the bottom line with a monthly draw based on net revenue for each month. You guys keep the building in your names. You may want to look at the third paragraph on the second page.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Just tell us,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Okay, there’s some pretty clear language about certain activities the new firm will not engage in. It will not pay bribes or referral fees to policemen, tow truck drivers, rescue personnel, or anyone else for case referrals. It will not advertise on bus stop benches, bingo cards, or any other cheap publication. In fact, all advertising must be approved by the Marketing Committee, which, at least for the first year, will consist solely of me. In other words, fellas, the firm will no longer chase ambulances.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What’s the fun of that?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’ve heard talk about advertising on billboards and television; that, too, is prohibited. Before the firm signs up a new client, the three of us must agree to take the case. In summary, the firm will adhere to the highest standards of professional conduct. Any fees in cash will go straight to the books, which will now be kept by a competent CPA. In effect, gentlemen, the new firm will operate like a real law firm. This agreement is good for one year, and if either of you fails to comply with it, then the partnership will dissolve and I’ll find work elsewhere.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Back to the attorneys’ fees,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I’m not sure you finished that part of the discussion.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “If we can agree on the rules of the new partnership, then I suggest we use the fees from the Khaing settlement to pay off the bank and clean up the Krayoxx mess, including the $15,000 in sanctions levied during the trial. That’s about $200,000. Rochelle gets a bonus of $100,000. That leaves $1.2 million for the lawyers, which I think we should divide equally.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You don’t have to do this, David.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I agree,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is your case. We’ve done nothing.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I understand,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “But I look at it like this: I would never have found this case had I not been here. It’s that simple. A year ago, I was working at a job I hated. By chance I stumbled into this place, met you guys, and then I got lucky and found this case.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Excellent point,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What about my divorce?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No problem. We have a signed settlement agreement. Your wife is not entitled to any fees earned after she signed it. The divorce will be final in January.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That’s the way I see it,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Me too,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Don’t even think about it,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Sorry. Force of habit,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “non-death”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “nice balance sheet,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown
